thread.document:
We were overwhelmed by the response to the Extra Credit Post --- we thought there would only be a few students interested.

In light of this, we are changing the nature of the extra credit to try a new experiment  --- so please ask clarification questions if anything isn't clear.


The new rules for extra credit are as follows. For each participation category there will be Blue Teams and Red Teams.

Red Team: The job of the Red Team is to establish a baseline. What is the best website that can be purely AI generated (with human guidance)? So be smart about how you prompt and thoughtful about the design, but code should be mostly AI written. Any analysis, summarization, grouping etc. should also be done by an AI. Meta level orchestrations is fine by a person. For instance, you can read a subset of the posts for validation purposes, but you should not read all the posts. It should be as though a human never looked at any of the posts or submissions to understand what they are doing. Ideally though there should be a functioning website that displays all content in a readable fashion. If you end up in a situation where it not possible to prompt engineer your way to fucntionality, put in the minimum human effort required to get this functioning and then document a short document/paragraph explaining what was done by an agent and where basic human intervention was necessary. All Red Team submissions will be awarded 4-5 points per student team member. Please feel free to ask clarification questions -- the goal of this is more to do a fun experiment than to be some ridiculous hoop that must be jumped through, we're very curious how far this can get! 


Blue Team: Your job is to do better than the Red Teams. You may use as much AI as you wish to help generate your website but we ask that you go beyond. Blue Teams will be awarded 5-10 points credit per student (based on staff judgement) if they can do better than the baseline. 


Note that these points are added to the total points in the course.


Please add yourself to the spreadsheet below so it will be easier to track the teams: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14QaSXdvKzj1UGRjPJ6-udmzQSB_UyyS5fl4-VvT6sLs/edit?gid=0#gid=0

Note: all the constraints in the earlier post still apply. Max team size is still 4 etc. 

https://edstem.org/us/courses/84647/discussion/7384785

Also note: You may only sign up for ONE team.

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>This can stream info on whether the posts are edited also, which should be checked to update your post entries or include post versioning, unless a forum has been archived (set to read-only)<break/><break/>This comes to mind because for those considering this API for future class use, for Ed Forums not set to: “Discussion is set to require approval for new threads”, in practice there has been the issue of webhooks catching posts that were accidentally posted public, removed, and then posted privately (or simply edited), resulting in TA’s reaching out to remove these. <break/><break/>Hope you find this helpful</paragraph></document>
comments.document:
